ad2.lead: Smart Truck (AD2 kit) is a commercial-vehicle ADAS kit, forward camera, radar, compute box, driver display and vehicle harness, sold at ₹2,50,000 into the Indian N2/N3 truck market. It is the single largest SKU in the DeepGrid portfolio, representing a management projection of ₹450 Cr and 39.9% of group FY2032 revenue from one product line.

useCases.title: Mandate compliance retrofit
useCases.buyer: Fleet operators and retrofit installers
useCases.problem: Fleet operators running N2/N3 trucks face a compliance-led obligation under the ADAS mandate requiring driver-drowsiness, blind-spot and lane-departure capabilities on their vehicles; the decision is not discretionary.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies the complete AD2 kit, camera, radar, compute and harness, through fleet-direct and retrofit installer channels, enabling fitment without waiting for OEM line-fit programmes.

useCases.title: OEM line-fit for new N2/N3 trucks
useCases.buyer: Truck OEMs and OEM homologation engineers
useCases.problem: Truck OEMs must equip every new N2/N3 vehicle with certified ADAS to satisfy the mandate, requiring a kit that has cleared ARAI or ICAT certification and can be integrated at the production line.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid offers the same AD2 architecture certified to AIS-162/188, sold to OEM or Tier-1 at the listed price, with the compute module designed for a direct swap to owned 28 nm silicon without requiring a vendor change.

useCases.title: Driver drowsiness and attention compliance
useCases.buyer: Fleet safety manager, OEM homologation engineer and testing-agency assessor
useCases.problem: Under AIS-184 (DDAWS) and CMVR 125Q(1), manufacturers must conduct a ten-participant day-and-night study generating ten or more true-positive or false-negative events and report per-participant sensitivity, approval is not a track test.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies an in-cab drowsiness pipeline covering eyelid closure, gaze, head pose and PERCLOS-class metrics fused with vehicle signals, together with the completed documentation package, metrics, thresholds, activation speed, weather limits and statistical analysis, that makes the submission approvable.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Camera and radar monitor the forward path and blind quarters; SoC2 fuses both sensor streams into a single object list carrying range and closing speed for every detected target. Collision, lane-departure and blind-spot logic then decide whether a warning is required, alerting the driver visually and acoustically, and signalling the brake interface where the vehicle supports it. The compute box accepts eleven inputs simultaneously, seven 8MP RGB cameras on GMSL2, two thermal cameras and front and rear 4D 77 GHz radar, completing sensor fusion in 8.6 ms of a 33.3 ms frame, leaving 74% of the frame budget unused. That headroom is what allows one hardware part to serve every sensor configuration below it in the product family.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The ADAS mandate imposes driver-drowsiness, blind-spot and lane-departure obligations on N2/N3 commercial vehicles, creating a compliance-driven demand pool that management estimates at 0.5 million new N2/N3 trucks per year plus 0.5 million retrofit units. The FY2032 target of 18,000 units represents a management assumption of 1.80% capture of that pool, making the revenue projection a floor tied to regulatory enforcement rather than a discretionary adoption curve. AIS-184 (DDAWS) obligations for new models begin 1 October 2027 and extend to all models from 1 January 2028, aligning with DeepGrid's first-revenue date of FY2027 and the volume ramp through FY2029. Certification through ARAI or ICAT is the gate that converts regulatory demand into bookable orders.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The kit is sold as a product at a fixed price of ₹2,50,000, held flat across all plan years, through fleet-direct, retrofit-installer and, over time, OEM line-fit channels. At 89% gross margin, a management projection, the economics depend on owning the compute silicon: the 28 nm SoC2 die allows the price to be held against imported alternatives while margin expands as FPGA-era bill-of-materials costs are replaced by the owned packaged part. The ramp is projected to reach 18,000 units and ₹450 Cr by FY2032, growing from 3 units in FY2027 through 80, 1,400, 4,000 and 9,000 in the intervening years. A software attach layer, T100 AI licensing, fleet data services and insurer integration, is planned as a subsequent revenue motion on the same hardware base, though those lines are accounted for separately in the plan.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Certification through ARAI or ICAT is the primary gate: without it the OEM line-fit channel, which is the volume engine, cannot open, and a delay also affects the AD0 Smart Mirror family sold to overlapping buyers, together those two SKUs represent ₹720 Cr of projected FY2032 revenue, more than the other thirteen SKUs combined. Installation channel capacity must scale to 18,000 fitments per year, a logistics and installer-network build that has no precedent in the current business. The ten-participant day-and-night drowsiness study required for AIS-184 approval must be completed and documented to a standard that a testing-agency assessor can act on, not merely demonstrated. ASP is held flat in the model, so any price erosion from competitive or channel pressure flows directly to margin with no volume offset built in.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹2,50,000, held flat across all plan years in the working model.
FY2032 revenue (management projection): ₹450 Cr, equal to 39.9% of group revenue, at 89% gross margin.

Demand pool (management assumption, pool sizes from third-party published estimates): 0.5 million new N2/N3 trucks per year plus 0.5 million retrofit; FY2032 volume of 18,000 units equals 1.80% capture.
Compute latency: SoC2 completes sensor fusion across eleven inputs in 8.6 ms of a 33.3 ms frame, leaving 74% of the frame budget unused.

taas.lead: Autonomous TaaS is a contracted Transport-as-a-Service line where DeepGrid provides the vehicle, autonomy stack and driver replacement as a metered service on fixed routes. It generates the highest revenue per unit in the portfolio at ₹66.00 L per vehicle, delivering an 89% gross margin on FY2032 revenue projected at ₹66 Cr.

useCases.title: Fixed-Route Haulage Operations
useCases.buyer: Logistics operators on fixed, repeatable routes where an autonomous lane can be proven
useCases.problem: Operators must lower cost per tonne-kilometre against a driven alternative on dedicated, repeatable corridors.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid delivers the complete vehicle, autonomy stack, route commissioning, and driver replacement billed per trip or per tonne.

useCases.title: Driver-Constrained Corridor Operations
useCases.buyer: Operators comparing against driver availability rather than driver cost
useCases.problem: On many freight routes, the primary operating constraint is finding a driver at all.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid provides autonomous transport service using the vehicle's full AD2 sensor set, SoC2 autonomy stack, and remote operations links.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The vehicle's full sensor set reads a fixed route that DeepGrid has surveyed beforehand, and SoC2 runs the autonomy perception and planning stack against that route model. Route plans are established by a fleet management system while vehicles operate autonomously within geofenced corridors under real-time monitoring via a fleet dashboard. Fleet logic manages routing and schedules hand-offs to a remote operator whenever conditions exceed what the onboard system should decide alone. The autonomy stack and SoC2 perception silicon remain technically identical to the AD2 kit, differing solely in commercial structure.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Logistics operators are commercially compelled to adopt TaaS when comparing cost per tonne-kilometre against conventional driven alternatives. Increasingly, the decision is driven by driver availability, because finding a driver at all has become the primary operational bottleneck on many routes. Deployments scale via direct commercial contracts executed one route at a time on proven autonomous lanes. DeepGrid targets capturing 100 units by FY2032, representing a 0.01% capture of the 0.6-0.8M units/yr India trucking demand pool.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Autonomous operations require regulatory clearance and route-level regulatory permissions to run inside controlled corridors. Because DeepGrid owns the vehicles, it absorbs direct operational risks around uptime that pure product sales avoid, necessitating reliable remote operator interventions. Fleet procurement depends on securing debt or lease asset finance against trucks of ~Rs60 Cr at an assumed 15% interest rate, rather than consuming equity round capital. DeepGrid must also successfully execute route commissioning and pre-surveys for each contracted corridor.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹66.00 L per vehicle, generating the highest revenue per unit across DeepGrid's portfolio (management projection).
FY2032 volume: 100 units, representing a 0.01% capture rate of the 0.6-0.8M units/yr India trucking demand pool (management projection).
Fleet debt: ~Rs60 Cr in TaaS fleet capex debt/lease financed against trucks at an assumed 15% interest rate (management projection).

ad0.lead: The AD0 Smart Mirror is an aftermarket replacement rear-view mirror system featuring an integrated display head unit, four surround body cameras, and a dedicated wiring loom. It serves as DeepGrid's initial volume ramp, with management projecting ₹270 Cr in FY2032 revenue (23.9% of total group revenue) across 54,000 units at an 89% gross margin.

useCases.title: Aftermarket passenger vehicle surround visibility
useCases.buyer: Vehicle owners via aftermarket accessory retail and fitment shops
useCases.problem: Vehicle owners seek to eliminate blind quarters and improve parking safety without costly vehicle modifications or waiting for factory-fitted systems.
useCases.delivers: A complete replacement mirror display unit with four surround cameras and a wiring loom that installs in an afternoon to provide full 360-degree stitched visibility.

useCases.title: Small fleet maneuvering safety and collision mitigation
useCases.buyer: Small fleet operators
useCases.problem: Fleet managers must minimize low-speed maneuvering damage and pedestrian incidents across operating fleets without grounding vehicles for extended installations.
useCases.delivers: An integrated unit combining SoC2 compute, recording storage, alert speaker, and motion logic that flags hazards entering blind quarters and issues directional driver alerts.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Four body cameras mounted around the vehicle continuously monitor blind quarters and feed raw video directly into the mirror-format head unit. DeepGrid's SoC2 silicon processes these incoming video streams under perception firmware, stitching the feeds into a unified 360° surround image. Integrated proximity and motion logic evaluates the unified scene in real time to detect any hazard penetrating defined danger zones. When a risk is detected, the driver sees the stitched visual feed on the mirror display and receives a directional audio alert from the onboard speaker.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: DeepGrid sells the AD0 Smart Mirror system at a fixed price of ₹50,000 through aftermarket accessory retail, independent fitment shops, and OEM accessory catalogues. Management projects revenue will expand from ₹0.05 Cr across 10 units in FY2027 to ₹270 Cr across 54,000 units in FY2032. The product delivers an 89% gross margin, contributing 23.9% of DeepGrid's projected group revenue in FY2032 by capturing 0.93% of the addressable surround-view market. Because of its low fitment complexity and broad consumer appeal, AD0 anchors the customer base expansion from 5 accounts in FY2027 to 650 accounts in FY2032.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The commercial model requires establishing broad distribution across accessory retail networks while maintaining unit pricing strictly at ₹50,000 without margin erosion. Fitment times must remain minimal, described alternately as an afternoon fitment or a 15-minute fitment, to ensure workshop throughput is not constrained. DeepGrid also faces significant portfolio concentration risk, as AD0 (₹270 Cr) and the Smart Truck kit (₹450 Cr) collectively represent ₹720 Cr or 64% of FY2032 projected revenue. Because these two road autonomy SKUs target overlapping market surfaces, any fitment or channel bottleneck directly imperils the larger part of the business plan.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹50,000, held flat across all projected operating years from FY2027 through FY2032.
FY2032 revenue (management projection): ₹270 Cr, representing 23.9% of total company revenue.
FY2032 unit volume (management projection): 54,000 units, the highest unit volume of any portfolio SKU.
Gross margin (management projection): 89% on product sales.

t100.lead: The T100 AI Licence is a pure software offering within the Silicon & Compute segment that licenses trained Indian road perception models, runtime toolchains, and update streams to third-party hardware platforms. It is the only product in the portfolio with no bill of materials, projected by management to generate ₹50 Cr at 94% gross margin in FY2032 as optionality without a separately sized demand pool.

useCases.title: Third-party automotive compute integration
useCases.buyer: OEMs and platform partners who want the India-road stack without our silicon
useCases.problem: OEMs seeking perception tuned for Indian traffic conditions, lane discipline, and lighting want to avoid spending three years collecting road datasets to train models themselves.
useCases.delivers: Trained India-road perception models, toolchain and deployment runtime, and continuous model update streams delivered via licence subscription to run on the customer's hardware.

useCases.title: Accountable integrator perception subsystem
useCases.buyer: accountable integrator
useCases.problem: Integrators must deploy a certified perception stack within their own system architecture while retaining their own brand, sensors, and compute hardware.
useCases.delivers: A bounded camera-perception subsystem that runs inference inside the customer's runtime, allowing the customer system to decide, act, and ship with DeepGrid perception inside.

detail.title: Deepgrid sells, and what it does not

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The customer operates their own compute hardware and sensors rather than purchasing physical silicon boards from DeepGrid. DeepGrid provides trained India-road perception models that execute inference inside the customer's deployment runtime. The customer's system handles decision-making and mechanical actuation, shipping the vehicle under their own brand. Ongoing model updates and support are delivered through a subscription licence, keeping perception aligned with Indian road conditions.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Foreign ADAS processors cannot be software-patched for Indian roads without collecting local data and retraining underlying models from scratch. Automotive teams want perception tuned for local traffic patterns and light without spending three years collecting datasets themselves. Revenue starts in FY2029 because an IP licence requires an operational track record before external platforms adopt it. Licensing the standalone software converts DeepGrid's proprietary Indian road dataset and model investments into a pure recurring revenue stream.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The licence sells at a unit price of ₹100.00 L through direct engagements negotiated per deployment. Because it delivers models and toolchains without any physical board or bill of materials, the line achieves a 94% gross margin, which is alternatively described as 90%+ in the investment memorandum. Management projections schedule volume ramping from 2 units (₹2 Cr) in FY29 to 6 in FY30, 18 in FY31, and 50 units (₹50.0 Cr) in FY32. Because no separately sized demand pool exists behind it in the demand schedule, management treats the ₹50 Cr revenue as optionality rather than a base case.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Commercialization depends on demonstrating a defensible model advantage and securing signed licence agreements, neither of which is evidenced yet. DeepGrid must prove maturity and build an operational track record for its perception stack before the FY2029 revenue start. Management must also manage the risk that licensing the standalone core could undercut its own full-stack systems business, which represents approximately 88% of planned revenue. Finally, sales must close directly with OEMs despite the absence of a separately sized demand pool in the business plan.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹100.00 L per licence deployment.
Gross margin: 94% (management projection; Investment Memorandum states 90%+).
FY2032 volume: 50 units (management projection; scaling from 2 units in FY29, 6 in FY30, and 18 in FY31).

useCases.title: Tier-1 Braking and Perception Subsystem Integration
useCases.buyer: Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs with in-house hardware teams
useCases.problem: Tier-1 suppliers must incorporate perception compute into custom boards inside an accountable safety case, wanting Indian-designed silicon and domestic supply rather than an imported module. DeepGrid does not own brake actuation, calibration, homologation, or warranty, leaving system-level responsibility with the integrator.

detail.title: Deepgrid sells, and what it does not

useCases.title: Commercial Vehicle OEM Hardware Integration
useCases.buyer: Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs with in-house hardware teams
useCases.problem: Vehicle manufacturers with internal engineering teams require domestic supply rather than an imported part, navigating direct design-in engagements where OEM design-in runs 18 to 30 months. They require bare silicon to place directly onto proprietary vehicle boards rather than buying an integrated module.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid provides the bare die with a datasheet and integration documentation, enabling customer sensors to feed their own board while SoC2 performs perception compute inside their design.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The product operates across a four-stage signal chain where the customer's own sensors feed their own board, the SoC2 die executes perception compute inside their design, their software decides what to do with the result, and their product ships with DeepGrid silicon inside. The silicon is designed for TSMC 28 nm with a die area of roughly 57 mm², running 32,768 MACs at 600 MHz for a derived 39.3 TOPS design target against 102.4 GB/s of dual-channel LPDDR5. DeepGrid delivers tested and binned silicon in tray or reel alongside reference design documentation and toolchain access, providing no enclosure, cables, or fitting. Because the buyer builds their own board and carries their own integration, DeepGrid provides bounded perception compute without absorbing vehicle-level engineering.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The ADAS mandate establishes legal compliance requirements for drowsiness, blind-spot, and lane-departure systems on commercial vehicles in India, creating an addressable pool of one million trucks a year that must comply. Incumbent implementations rely on imported modules costing three to eight thousand dollars a module, whereas DeepGrid's die costs three dollars and eighty-eight cents at volume, opening a significant domestic cost advantage. At the same time, vehicle manufacturers face public procurement policies favoring domestic supply and seek Indian-designed silicon rather than imported components. Because OEM design-in runs 18 to 30 months before qualified volume silicon lands in H1 2028, manufacturers must enter direct design-in engagements immediately to prepare their production boards.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Product viability depends entirely on working, qualified silicon downstream of ASIC tapeout completion and qualification. Because bare die sales provide no enclosure or integration layer, every unit in this line is downstream of the tapeout landing. DeepGrid must secure direct design-in engagements with Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs with in-house hardware teams through long cycles and high commitment, where OEM design-in runs 18 to 30 months. DeepGrid must also provide sufficient reference designs and toolchain support so integrators execute their own software without requiring broad OEM customisation or safety-case ownership from DeepGrid.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹18,000 (management projection).
FY2032 volume and revenue: 30,000 units generating ₹54 Cr (4.8% of the plan) at 94% gross margin (management projection).
Silicon design specifications: TSMC 28 nm, roughly 57 mm², 32,768 MACs at 600 MHz for a derived 39.3 TOPS design target, against 102.4 GB/s of dual-channel LPDDR5.
Market capture: 0.25% capture at FY2032 India ADAS chip pool, based on an EMR 2024 estimate of $2.29B at 20.6% CAGR (management projection).

ad1.lead: The AD1 Indoor L4 Kit is a self-driving retrofit kit, comprising a sensor head, SoC2 compute box, and drive-by-wire actuation interface, designed to convert existing forklifts and tugs into closed-loop autonomous vehicles. Because it operates inside private sites exempt from automotive homologation, it allows DeepGrid to ship commercial Level-4 autonomy years before public-road deployment while serving as the technical proof point for the road roadmap.

useCases.title: Warehouse and Dark-Store Intralogistics
useCases.buyer: Warehouse and industrial operators
useCases.problem: Operators need to automate repetitive internal material movement, including inbound put-away and pick runs across busy floors, using forklifts and tugs the site already owns.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies a retrofit kit featuring camera and depth sensing, an onboard SoC2 compute box, and drive-by-wire actuation that executes closed-loop steering, throttle, and braking with auto-rerouting.

useCases.title: Material-Handling System Integration
useCases.buyer: Material-handling integrators
useCases.problem: Integrators require turnkey autonomous drive-by-wire and perception packages to automate customer-owned indoor utility fleets without waiting for public-road homologation frameworks.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid provides the complete sensor suite, 24 m LiDAR and camera fusion pipeline, site mapping tooling, and ±5 cm obstacle stop actuation to operate reliably within geofenced indoor zones.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The AD1 Indoor L4 Kit executes a closed-loop signal chain across four continuous stages: sensing, SoC2 onboard computation, decision-making, and actuation. A 24 m LiDAR running at 5 Hz and a 57° camera fuse depth and visual sensing into a single bird’s-eye occupancy view that detects aisles, loads, and workers. The SoC2 processor localizes the vehicle against a pre-commissioned site map stored directly onboard, allowing an integrated planner to determine path and speed within a dynamic geofenced safety zone at up to 1.5 m/s or ≤25 km/h. Finally, a drive-by-wire actuation interface directly commands steering, throttle, and braking to guarantee closed-loop control and obstacle stopping within ±5 cm.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Operating inside private industrial and warehouse facilities exempts AD1 from public-road automotive homologation rules, turning vehicle automation into an immediate commercial procurement decision. This regulatory asymmetry allows DeepGrid to deploy fully closed-loop Level-4 autonomous behaviour years before public-road autonomy is legally permitted in India. Deploying AD1 early also validates the 28 nm SoC2 architecture and production perception stack under real-world operating conditions, serving as the live technical proof point for the broader road autonomy portfolio. Furthermore, the retrofit form factor targets existing material-handling fleets directly without requiring operators to replace capital equipment.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The primary operational bottleneck for AD1 expansion is site mapping and commissioning throughput, which depends on field services capacity rather than pure silicon product availability. DeepGrid must also ensure that its drive-by-wire actuation interfaces seamlessly integrate across diverse third-party industrial vehicle models already owned by customer sites. Operationally, the software decision layer must reliably resolve dense real-world hazards, such as spills, peer automated guided vehicles, and workers, utilizing preset stuck-time auto-rerouting to prevent floor deadlocks. Scaling to 4,200 annual units by FY2032 also requires sustained distribution traction through third-party material-handling integrators.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹1,00,000 (also listed as ₹1.00 L) per retrofit kit.
FY2032 revenue: ₹42 Cr (3.7% of plan, 4,200 units; management projection).
Gross margin: 89% in portfolio projections, compared to an ASIC gross margin of ~80% and an FPGA gross margin of ~67% in memorandum estimates (management projections).
Closed-loop operating envelope: Planning at up to 1.5 m/s (also specified as ≤25 km/h) with a ±5 cm obstacle stop, powered by a 24 m LiDAR at 5 Hz and a 57° camera.

a100-4.lead: The A100 Compute Box 4ch PCIe is a four-camera PCIe card carrying DeepGrid's SoC2, sold to OEMs and integrators who need full surround perception inside their own host architecture. At ₹3,00,000 it is the highest-priced compute SKU in the portfolio, with an 89% gross margin and management-projected FY2032 revenue of ₹36 Cr at 1,200 units.

useCases.title: Multi-camera automotive edge-AI
useCases.buyer: OEMs and integrators running complete multi-camera stacks on their own platform
useCases.problem: These buyers need full surround perception across four camera feeds but want to integrate the compute into their own host architecture rather than adopt a turnkey system.
useCases.delivers: A PCIe card carrying the SoC2 with four camera inputs, an SDK and model toolchain, and structured object lists output to the host over PCIe, so the integrator builds its own product on top without designing its own board.

useCases.title: Industrial inspection and infrastructure monitoring
useCases.buyer: OEMs and integrators
useCases.problem: Industrial inspection and infrastructure monitoring applications require simultaneous multi-camera perception at high utilisation without the cost or complexity of a custom board design.
useCases.delivers: The A100 4ch card runs parallel perception across all four streams on the SoC2, with each compute cube maintaining its own local DMA against an eight-bank L2 to keep utilisation high, then passes results to the host system.

useCases.title: Security and surveillance compute
useCases.buyer: OEMs and integrators
useCases.problem: Security and infrastructure monitoring deployments demand multi-camera coverage with on-card compute so that the host system receives processed alerts rather than raw video streams.
useCases.delivers: Up to four camera feeds enter via the PCIe interface; the SoC2 runs parallel perception on all four channels and outputs object lists and alerts to the host, with the customer's software consuming structured perception data directly.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Four cameras feed into the card via PCIe, providing full surround coverage; the SoC2 runs perception across all four streams simultaneously and returns structured results to the host over the same PCIe interface. The memory architecture is central to why four channels is feasible at high utilisation: each compute cube runs its own local DMA against an eight-bank L2, avoiding the throughput bottleneck of a single global DMA path. The host system provides the enclosure, thermal management and power, and builds its own product on top of the structured output. This dependency on host thermal and power budget is the primary constraint on which customers can adopt the card.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The card enters revenue in FY2028, the same year the broader ASIC-era product wave reaches market following SoC2 tapeout, making it part of a nine-SKU cohort that switches on simultaneously. The addressed market is the automotive edge-AI accelerator modules segment, sized at $4.8B in 2025 and projected by Dataintelo at $22.6B by 2034 at a 21% CAGR; the FY2032 volume of 1,200 units represents a 0.20% capture of that pool, which is a management assumption against a third-party published estimate. OEMs and integrators are increasingly designing multi-camera perception into their own platforms rather than buying complete systems, creating demand for a high-capacity compute component that does not require custom silicon work. The PCIe form factor aligns with standard host architectures, lowering the integration barrier for larger design-in customers reached through a direct channel.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: At ₹3,00,000 per unit and an 89% gross margin, the A100 4ch PCIe is the highest-priced compute SKU in the portfolio and the one that generates the most revenue per unit sold across the compute-box ladder. Management projects revenue doubling each year from ₹2 Cr at 75 units in FY2028 to ₹36 Cr at 1,200 units in FY2032, a consistent doubling cadence that reflects design-in cycles rather than volume consumer ramp. The 89% gross margin is consistent with the other compute-box SKUs and with the Smart Truck and Indoor L4 kit, reflecting the absence of low-margin sensor or mechanical content. The card is sold direct to larger integrators via design-in, which keeps channel cost low and supports margin preservation at relatively modest unit volumes.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The foundational dependency is ASIC tapeout and PCIe interface validation; without a functioning SoC2 die, no compute-box SKU ships, and the A100 4ch PCIe is among the nine products gated by that milestone. Host thermal and power budget is the second constraint: customers whose enclosures cannot accommodate the card's requirements are excluded from the addressable pool, limiting the market to integrators with sufficient platform headroom. The direct design-in channel means revenue is concentrated in a small number of larger integrators, so a delay or cancellation in any one design-in has an outsized effect on the FY2028–FY2030 ramp. Volume at 1,200 units by FY2032 remains modest in absolute terms, so the business case depends on margin rather than scale, and any erosion of the ₹3,00,000 price point would materially affect the revenue line.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹3,00,000, the highest price point in the compute-box ladder and the highest-priced compute SKU in the portfolio.
FY2032 revenue (management projection): ₹36 Cr at 1,200 units, representing 3.2% of group revenue at an 89% gross margin.

Demand pool (third-party estimate, Dataintelo): Automotive edge-AI accelerator modules $4.8B in 2025, projected to $22.6B by 2034 at a 21% CAGR; FY2032 volume of 1,200 units is a management assumption of 0.20% capture.

dhumr.lead: Defence D-HUMR is a defence-grade unmanned ground vehicle platform engineered with hardened compute, encrypted communications, and a ruggedised sensor suite for outdoor reconnaissance and logistics. Priced at ₹20,00,000 per unit, it represents the highest price point across DeepGrid's portfolio and serves as an early sovereign revenue stream independent of automotive mandates.

useCases.title: Defence Logistics and Unmanned Reconnaissance
useCases.buyer: Indian Army and MoD procurement programmes
useCases.problem: The military requires autonomous logistics and reconnaissance platforms for hazardous missions where sending an unmanned ground vehicle is preferable to risking human personnel. Operating environments often feature GPS-denied conditions and complex terrain requiring secure, encrypted operational integrity.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid delivers an unmanned ground vehicle featuring surround sensing, an autonomy stack running on SoC2 with military-grade encryption, autonomous navigation in GPS-denied environments, a teleoperation link, and a secure command post data relay.

useCases.title: Intelligent Perimeter Threat Fusion
useCases.buyer: Defence/Paramilitary organisations (DRDO/MCEME pipeline)
useCases.problem: Perimeter security requires identifying coordinated breach threats across access boundaries without flooding security operators with nuisance false alarms that cause surveillance systems to be disabled.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies an outward-facing multi-sensor fusion stack (proven via the DGrid Sentinel console) that correlates external vehicle tracks and fence-line human movements along a timed threat ladder, holding benign tracks while explaining escalation rationale in words.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Defence D-HUMR operates on a four-stage signal chain consisting of sense, compute on SoC2, decide, and act. Surround sensing using ruggedised camera, radar, and thermal sensors reads the surrounding terrain, obstacles, and personnel, pointing the fusion stack outward rather than forward. The SoC2 processor classifies and correlates individual sensor tracks, constructs a local map, and plans traversable paths with military-grade encryption. The vehicle executes autonomous navigation even in GPS-denied operational domains, while maintaining a teleoperation link and secure relays back to the command post.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Armed forces are actively shifting toward autonomous platforms for hazardous logistics and reconnaissance where deploying robotic vehicles is preferred over exposing personnel. Indian defence procurement pipelines via iDEX, DRDO, and MCEME enforce indigenous-preference rules that structurally bar import-dependent foreign competitors. Furthermore, early validation on FPGA hardware has already demonstrated revenue traction, enabling the company to tap government procurement channels and GeM listings without waiting for automotive regulatory deadlines.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Commercial scale hinges on navigating slow, multi-year defence procurement cycles and securing mandatory military security clearances. Management must resolve background intellectual property ownership, as past delivered revenue of ₹23.01L resided in a separate legal entity with IP owned by MCEME. DeepGrid must also successfully transition its early FPGA platform to qualified production silicon without procurement delays disrupting lumpy defense order intake.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹20,00,000 per Defence D-HUMR platform.
FY2032 revenue: ₹30 Cr management projection (representing 2.7% of the total plan).
FY2032 volume: 150 units shipped management projection (ramping from 6 units in FY2027).

a100-2.lead: The A100 Compute Box 2ch is a dual-channel compute board that runs stereo or wide-field camera perception on a single SoC2 die, returning a fused object list to the customer's host system. At ₹1,60,000 and 89% gross margin, it is the volume centre of DeepGrid's compute line, with management projecting ₹28.8 Cr revenue at 1,800 units by FY2032.

useCases.title: Reversing with side detection
useCases.buyer: Integrators building multi-camera perception without taking DeepGrid's full kit
useCases.problem: A vehicle or platform needs simultaneous rear and side awareness during low-speed manoeuvres, but a four-channel surround system is more than the application requires.
useCases.delivers: Two camera inputs processed on one SoC2 produce a fused near-field output covering both views, returned to the integrator's own application without requiring a full surround compute stack.

useCases.title: Two-camera inspection rig
useCases.buyer: Integrators building multi-camera perception without taking DeepGrid's full kit
useCases.problem: Industrial or logistics inspection systems need to reconcile two views of the same scene into a single object list, a task a single-channel module cannot perform and a four-channel card would over-provision.
useCases.delivers: The board runs perception on both streams simultaneously on one SoC2 and returns a fused output, using the hardware transformer path that the two-channel configuration is the first to justify over a general-purpose processor.

useCases.title: Small autonomous platform
useCases.buyer: Integrators building multi-camera perception without taking DeepGrid's full kit
useCases.problem: A compact autonomous platform requires stereo or dual-angle perception for navigation but cannot accommodate the cost or board space of a four-channel PCIe card.
useCases.delivers: The A100 2ch board provides stereo-pair or wider-field dual-stream perception with host integration, sold direct or through electronics distribution, at a price point positioned as roughly double the single-channel SKU for twice the channels.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Two cameras feed the board either as a stereo pair or covering a wider combined field; the board runs perception on both streams in parallel on a single SoC2 die and returns a fused output to the customer's host application, which then acts on it. Two channels is the first configuration where fusion across views becomes necessary, requiring the hardware transformer path built into the SoC2 rather than a general-purpose processor. The signal chain follows the same four-stage pattern as every DeepGrid product, sense, compute, decide, act, and uses the same toolchain and SDK as the single-channel entry SKU, so no additional certification path is required. The board includes camera input harnessing and the model toolchain, making it a self-contained module rather than a bare semiconductor.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: The product's first revenue is FY2028, the year the ASIC era begins for DeepGrid: all nine FY2028 SKUs are gated by the SoC2 tapeout, and FY2027 revenue across the portfolio is FPGA-based only. The addressed demand pool is the automotive edge-AI accelerator modules market, sized at $4.8B in 2025 and projected by Dataintelo at $22.6B by 2034 at a 21% CAGR; these are third-party published estimates and the capture rates are management assumptions. The A100 2ch targets integrators who need more than one camera view but not a full surround system, a segment that grows as multi-camera architectures become standard in automotive and industrial autonomy. FY2032 volume of 1,800 units represents a 0.20% capture of that pool, a management projection.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The unit price is ₹1,60,000 and gross margin is 89%, consistent with the compute-box line and the broader silicon-and-compute segment, which excludes lower-margin sensor and defence SKUs. Revenue ramps from 113 units and approximately ₹1.81 Cr in FY2028 to 1,800 units and ₹28.8 Cr in FY2032, doubling each year through FY2031 before reaching the plan target. The product is sold direct and through electronics distribution, avoiding the installation and warranty logistics that compress margins on system-level products. At 2.5% of group FY2032 revenue, it is a mid-tier contributor, positioned as a step on a compute ladder that lets one die address multiple price points rather than a standalone destination.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The single most critical dependency is the SoC2 ASIC tapeout: without it, no FY2028 revenue begins for this SKU or any of the eight other products scheduled to launch that year. The toolchain shared with the single-channel SKU is an advantage for cost, but it also means a toolchain problem affects multiple products simultaneously. Volume growth assumes integrators adopt dual-camera architectures at the projected rate; buyers who find the four-channel card wasteful and the single channel insufficient must exist in sufficient numbers to reach 1,800 units by FY2032, which is a management assumption against a third-party market estimate. Distribution through electronics channels adds a route-to-market dependency that is separate from the silicon risk.

FY2032 revenue: ₹28.8 Cr at 1,800 units, representing 2.5% of group revenue, management projection.

a100-1.lead: The A100 Compute Box 1ch M.2 is a single-channel M.2 module carrying DeepGrid's SoC2 die, the lowest-cost entry point into the platform at ₹85,000, designed to drop into a customer's existing carrier board without requiring them to design hardware around a bare die. At 89% gross margin and a management-projected ₹25.5 Cr by FY2032, it is the widest top of the compute funnel and the cheapest way any customer can adopt DeepGrid perception.

useCases.title: Integrator prototyping
useCases.buyer: Integrators prototyping single-camera products
useCases.problem: Product teams need to evaluate DeepGrid's SoC2 and toolchain without committing to a full board design around a bare die, which requires hardware engineering resources they may not have.
useCases.delivers: An M.2 module carrying the SoC2, an SDK and model toolchain, and reference carrier documentation that lets the integrator self-serve the design-in into their existing enclosure and sensor.

useCases.title: Single-camera product build
useCases.buyer: Integrators building genuinely single-camera products
useCases.problem: Customers building products that require exactly one camera channel of perception need a compute module sized and priced for that scope, not a multi-channel board they cannot fully utilise.
useCases.delivers: One camera feeds the customer's carrier board; the M.2 module runs their model on the SoC2; results return over the bus to their application, which then acts on the output.

useCases.title: AEBS forward-path perception
useCases.buyer: Tier-1 ADAS system engineer, functional-safety manager, OEM chief engineer
useCases.problem: AIS-162 / IS 11852:2019 under CMVR Rule 96(12) obliges M2/M3/N2/N3 vehicles to carry AEBS with a warning issued at least 1.4 s before braking and no emergency phase before TTC 3.0 s, a perception budget the Tier-1 must satisfy.
useCases.delivers: Detection, classification, tracking and per-target TTC on a documented interface with confidence and sensor-health state; actuation, calibration, homologation and warranty remain with the Tier-1.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The signal chain follows four stages: one camera feeds the customer's carrier board; the M.2 module runs the customer's model on the SoC2; results return over the bus to their application; and their product acts on the output. The module uses the same die as every other product in the portfolio, it is simply the same part running less, configured for one camera channel. Because the customer already owns the enclosure and the sensor, the integration surface is narrow: the M.2 interface and the software toolchain. That self-serve model means toolchain quality and documentation are the primary technical dependency, not hardware integration support from DeepGrid.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: First revenue is projected for FY2028, the year the ASIC era begins, FY2027 revenue across the portfolio is FPGA-based product only, and the A100 M.2 module requires the SoC2 tapeout to ship. The addressable pool is the automotive edge-AI accelerator module market, sized at $4.8B in 2025 and projected by Dataintelo at $22.6B by 2034 at a 21% CAGR; these are third-party published estimates and the capture rates are management assumptions. The product's specific trigger is customers who want the silicon and toolchain without designing a board around a bare die, a need that grows as more integrators seek to add perception to existing products rather than build from scratch. The ADAS mandate (AIS-162) coming into force for new models from 1 January 2027 and all models from 1 October 2027 creates a near-term demand pull for perception-capable compute modules among Tier-1 integrators.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The unit price is ₹85,000, held flat across the plan period, with a gross margin of 89%, the same margin as the other A100 compute box variants and the main autonomous-systems SKUs. Management projects 188 units in FY2028 rising to 3,000 units in FY2032, generating ₹25.5 Cr in that year, which is 2.3% of group revenue. The module is sold direct and through electronics distribution, converting what would otherwise be a semiconductor sale into a module sale for customers without a hardware team, and capturing margin on packaging, SDK and documentation rather than requiring DeepGrid to own installation or warranty. Its role in the portfolio is explicitly the widest top of the compute funnel, a low-friction entry point intended to pull customers toward higher-channel and higher-value SKUs.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: The single most critical dependency is the ASIC tapeout: no SoC2 silicon means no module, and all nine FY2028 SKUs share this gate. Because the buyer self-serves, toolchain quality and documentation must be sufficient for an integrator to complete a design-in without hands-on support from DeepGrid, a failure here raises support costs and slows adoption. For the AEBS use case specifically, a braking Tier-1 must accept the perception interface, diagnostics, safety assumptions and validation plan in writing with a recorded go/no-go, and no published ISO 26262 pathway yet exists, meaning an assessor must be engaged before the integrator can compare DeepGrid against a certified incumbent. Capital release is conditioned on partner access, field telemetry and a primary qualification artifact clearing together.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹85,000, held flat across the plan period; gross margin 89% (management projection).
Volume ramp (management projection): 188 units FY2028 → 375 FY2029 → 750 FY2030 → 1,500 FY2031 → 3,000 FY2032.
Market pool: Automotive edge-AI accelerator modules $4.8B (2025), projected $22.6B by 2034 at 21% CAGR (Dataintelo); FY2032 volume of 3,000 units represents 0.20% capture, a management assumption.
FY2032 revenue: ₹25.5 Cr (management projection), 2.3% of group revenue; first revenue FY2028.

agv.lead: The Seaport AGV is an autonomous container yard vehicle designed to transport shipping containers between quay cranes and yard blocks within port perimeters. It carries the second-highest unit price in the portfolio at ₹45,30,000 with an 89% gross margin and has achieved external validation through a live order at Vizag Container Terminal.

useCases.title: Quay-to-yard container transfer
useCases.buyer: Port and terminal operators
useCases.problem: Terminal operators need to transfer containers reliably between quay cranes and yard blocks inside a geofenced site while lowering labour costs and expanding throughput.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid provides an autonomous container yard vehicle equipped with surround sensing, SoC2 compute, yard management integration, and centimetre-level positioning.

useCases.title: Constrained campus cargo automation
useCases.buyer: Regional seaports and industrial campuses
useCases.problem: Campus operators must automate heavy cargo-handling equipment under low speed limits and controlled traffic conditions.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid implements proof-of-concept AGV deployments running real-time sensor fusion to handle cargo in live operating environments.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: Surround sensing detects containers, cranes, travel lanes, and yard personnel, feeding raw inputs into the SoC2 to localise against the yard map and track moving obstacles. Under quay cranes where satellite positioning degrades, dynamic sensor fusion on the SoC2 maintains 7 cm accuracy in the open and 22 cm under cranes where RTK-GNSS alone fails. The onboard planner sequences pick, transit, and drop tasks against terminal dispatch schedules, autonomously actuating steering, throttle, and braking. During commissioning, the system runs alongside the existing terminal system in shadow mode before receiving control, ensuring crane-synchronised dispatch without disruption.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Terminal operators face escalating pressures to optimise container throughput and lower operating labour costs within controlled, geofenced facilities. Because terminal operations take place off public roads, adoption does not depend on public-road homologation, allowing operational performance rather than regulatory mandates to drive deployment. The automated container terminal market was valued at $10.95B in 2024 and is projected to reach $16.35B by 2032 at a 5.2% CAGR. Securing early AGV deployments provides immediate high-margin contract cash flow and operational data that de-risks custom silicon tape-out.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: DeepGrid sells directly to terminal operators, typically entering berths through a pilot deployment before scaling across the terminal. Product dossiers list the unit price at ₹45,30,000 with an 89% gross margin, whereas the Investment Memorandum describes the model as fleet operations priced at ₹45.3L per AGV per year with a 92% gross margin. Management projections target FY2032 revenue of ₹22.6 Cr across 50 units, contributing 2.0% of total group revenue. Projected shipments scale from 2 units in FY2028 (₹0.91 Cr) to 50 units in FY2032 (₹22.65 Cr), capturing an assumed 0.02% of the total terminal automation pool.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Commercial rollout depends on formal port authority partnerships and domain certification. Berth-level commissioning and yard management system integration are bespoke, slow processes that dictate field installation velocity. DeepGrid must demonstrate in shadow-mode trials that sensor fusion holds accuracy under cranes and reduces crane idle times. Expanding the business requires converting initial proof points, such as the live order at Vizag Container Terminal, into recurring, multi-unit fleet orders.

facts.text: Unit price: Listed at ₹45,30,000 (also reported as ₹45.30 L) per vehicle platform.
FY2032 revenue (management projection): ₹22.6 Cr (also recorded as ₹22.65 Cr), representing 2.0% of plan revenue.
FY2032 volume (management projection): 50 units shipped.

d100.lead: The D100 Drone SoC Kit is an aerial compute and perception package designed for airframe builders, integrating a flight-weight SoC2 module, sensing set, flight-controller interface, and airborne software development kit. It opens aerial perception markets using DeepGrid's common silicon die with minimal incremental engineering, delivering a management-projected ₹20 Cr in FY2032 revenue at a 68% gross margin.

useCases.title: Tactical defence drone autonomy
useCases.buyer: Defence drone manufacturers and military airframe builders
useCases.problem: Airframes operating in contested operational theaters face intense GPS jamming along borders such as the Line of Control and cannot rely on vulnerable radio communication links to navigate safely.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies a single-die compute module running visual-inertial odometry, obstacle avoidance, and deterministic flight control, serving as a hardware fail-safe that flies the aircraft autonomously when external signals fail.

useCases.title: Commercial aerial inspection and surveillance
useCases.buyer: Commercial drone manufacturers
useCases.problem: Commercial airframe builders require onboard perception for inspection and survey tasks where remote control signals drop out or radio latency compromises flight safety.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid provides a flight-capable kit integrating gimbal camera and thermal sensor interfaces with SoC2 airborne perception to perform real-time visual odometry, object detection, and tracking.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The D100 kit executes an onboard four-stage signal chain comprising sensing, compute, planning, and flight-control actuation. Cameras, thermal sensors, and an inertial measurement unit feed raw scene and airframe motion data directly into the SoC2 module. The processor executes visual odometry and perception in real time to generate waypoints and avoidance manoeuvres for the airframe's flight controller. Housing visual-inertial navigation, perception, and flight control on a unified die eliminates inter-chip bus latency and reduces weight, ensuring deterministic fail-safe recovery if communication links drop.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Modern military and industrial missions increasingly operate in environments where electronic jamming or physical line-of-sight obstructions prevent reliance on ground-based radio links. Drones must therefore calculate their own positioning and safety decisions locally on the airframe rather than depending on vulnerable telemetry. DeepGrid capitalises on this demand, tracked in the edge-AI drone market growing at an 18% CAGR, because airborne perception shares the core algorithms of its ground automotive stack with the ground removed. This enables the company to enter an expanding robotics market ahead of automotive timelines without the capital expenditure of taping out new silicon.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: DeepGrid must strictly manage physical weight and electrical power budgets, which are far tighter for airborne platforms than for ground vehicles. Commercial scaling also depends on the maturation of domestic drone regulations and compatible airframe form factors across commercial and defence sectors. The engineering team must maintain low-latency, deterministic integration between the perception stack and third-party flight controllers to prevent in-flight failures. Finally, executive leadership must treat the SKU as high-margin strategic optionality while navigating defence procurement cycles.

FY2032 volume: 400 units (management projection).

thermal.lead: The Thermal Camera Pod is a bolt-on long-wave infrared sensor module with an integrated lens heater and weatherised housing that feeds into the SoC2 compute box. Serving as the perception layer for night and monsoon operation, management projects the product to generate ₹16.0 Cr in FY2032 revenue at a 50% gross margin as a capability line closing the condition where visible cameras are weakest.

useCases.title: Aftermarket Fleet Night and Monsoon Retrofit
useCases.buyer: Fleets upgrading existing vehicles
useCases.problem: Commercial vehicle fleets face sharp perception degradation when operating visible-light cameras through night, monsoon rain, glare, dust, and smoke.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid supplies a bolt-on long-wave infrared sensor module with a weatherised housing, lens heater, and harness that connects to the SoC2 compute box to detect emitted heat from people and animals.

useCases.title: Smart Truck ADAS Tower Integration
useCases.buyer: OEM cab and body engineer, Tier-1 HMI owner, and fleet safety officer
useCases.problem: Heavy commercial vehicles require continuous blind-spot and moving-off monitoring under AIS-186 and AIS-187 without high nuisance alert rates when visibility conditions collapse.
useCases.delivers: DeepGrid integrates thermal sensing into retrofit mirror towers as one of eleven fused perception channels feeding directly into the SoC2 object list.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The Thermal Camera Pod integrates an LWIR thermal sensor, dedicated lens, and weatherised housing with a lens heater that connects via harness into the SoC2 compute box. Because the LWIR sensor reads emitted heat rather than reflected light, a person or animal appears bright against a cold road through unlit conditions, glare, dust, and smoke. DeepGrid's SoC2 silicon executes detection on the thermal image, classifies people and animals from roadside clutter, and routes detections into the common object list fed by visible cameras. In the truck kit layout, the thermal pod operates as one of eleven fused channels across mirror towers, maintaining vehicle perception when optical cameras fail.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Optical camera detection degrades sharply during night and monsoon conditions, leaving heavy transport operators vulnerable on unlit roads. Safety standards such as AIS-186 and AIS-187 require reliable near-field blind-spot and moving-off information, mandating warnings before potential collisions with vulnerable road users. The Thermal Camera Pod closes this critical visibility gap by sensing emitted heat without requiring changes to the underlying SoC2 compute box architecture. Commercial fleets can deploy the pod as an aftermarket attach alongside AD0 and AD2 kits at the same fitment as the base kit.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: Management projects the Thermal Camera Pod to generate ₹16.0 Cr in FY2032 revenue from annual shipments of 3,200 units, representing 1.4% of total group revenue. The unit price is ₹50,000, with first revenue scheduled for FY2027. Sold into the aftermarket as an attach alongside AD0 and AD2 kits, the product captures a secondary sale from fleets upgrading existing vehicles. Management projects a 50% gross margin, operating the product as a capability line rather than a primary profit driver to close the conditions where core optical products are weakest.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: DeepGrid depends on imported thermal sensor supply, which represents the highest bill-of-materials risk in the sensor group. The engineering team must maintain a robust sensor sourcing and calibration pipeline to reliably fuse thermal detections with visible camera feeds. In commercial vehicle deployments, DeepGrid operates strictly as a bounded camera-perception subsystem, requiring measured false-information testing and qualification through independent testing agencies such as ARAI or ICAT.

FY2032 revenue: ₹16.0 Cr, representing 1.4% of group revenue (management projection).
FY2032 volume: 3,200 units, representing 0.10% capture of the $1.68B global automotive thermal camera market in 2025 (management projection).
Gross margin: 50% (management projection).

h100.lead: The H100 Driver Monitor is an alertness and fatigue tracking hardware SKU, configured as an on-body sensing wristband or an in-cabin monitoring unit, powered by DeepGrid's 28 nm SoC2 silicon. Positioned at ₹5,000 as DeepGrid's lowest-priced hardware offering, management projects it to generate ₹10 Cr in FY2032 (0.9% of group revenue at a 50% gross margin) to serve as a channel opener for fleet customer acquisition rather than a standalone profit line.

useCases.title: Commercial fleet driver alertness monitoring
useCases.buyer: Fleets meeting drowsiness obligations without fitting a cabin camera
useCases.problem: Fleet operators must comply with mandatory driver drowsiness monitoring regulations while managing driver resistance to intrusive in-cabin video surveillance.
useCases.delivers: A wrist-worn band with photoplethysmography (PPG) and motion sensing, an on-device fatigue model scoring alertness locally without transmitting raw data, and a direct radio link into the vehicle alert chain.

useCases.title: Automotive homologation for driver drowsiness systems
useCases.buyer: OEM homologation engineer and testing-agency assessor
useCases.problem: Vehicle manufacturers require type approval under AIS-184 (DDAWS) and CMVR 125Q(1), which mandates empirical testing demonstrating compliance across both daytime and nighttime conditions.
useCases.delivers: An in-cabin drowsiness processing pipeline paired with an assessable ten-participant day-and-night documentation study reporting per-participant sensitivity and standard deviation.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: In its wearable configuration, the H100 driver monitor utilizes an on-body wristband with photoplethysmography (PPG) and motion sensing to continuously monitor driver pulse and movement. An on-device fatigue model running on DeepGrid's shared SoC2 silicon evaluates alertness locally, preserving driver privacy by scoring fatigue states without broadcasting raw biometric data. When measured fatigue crosses a predefined threshold, the device connects via radio to the vehicle alert chain to warn the driver and notify the fleet. In the alternate in-cabin unit specification, an infrared camera tracks the driver's face, eyelid closure, gaze, and head pose, while the H100 bio-ADC processes steering torque and cabin biometrics.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Commercial vehicle operators face mandatory compliance deadlines under the ADAS mandate, specifically AIS-184 for Driver Drowsiness and Attention Warning Systems (DDAWS) under CMVR 125Q(1), alongside international regulations such as EU Reg 2021/267. Fleets actively seek lower-intrusion monitoring alternatives because optical in-cab cameras encounter driver resistance and acceptance hurdles. DeepGrid addresses this operational friction by offering a wearable band that tracks physiological metrics directly rather than recording the cabin environment. This regulatory inflection creates an immediate opening for DeepGrid to establish direct-to-fleet relationships using its lowest-priced hardware product.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: DeepGrid sells the H100 direct to fleets at a price of ₹5,000, though one product description states Fifteen hundred rupees. Management projects volume reaching 20,000 units in FY2032, generating ₹10 Cr (also recorded as ₹10.0 Cr, representing 0.9% or 0.89% of group revenue) at a 50% gross margin. Positioned as the lowest-priced item at ₹5,000, DeepGrid treats it as a channel line to establish fleet relationships rather than a profit line. Once deployed, the hardware anchors recurring software revenue, including fleet-health SaaS at ₹8L/truck/yr and tiered compliance subscriptions at ₹15,000 / year per vehicle.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: For the wearable product to succeed, fleets must maintain operational enrolment discipline and secure driver acceptance regarding wearing and charging the device. For camera-based vehicle integrations, DeepGrid must successfully clear the testing-agency gate by delivering an assessable ten-participant day-and-night evaluation showing compliant sensitivity metrics. Commercial scale is fundamentally dependent on the implementation and enforcement timeline of the ADAS mandate across commercial trucks and buses. If regulatory inspection and enforcement slip, commercial transport fleets may defer adoption of dedicated driver monitoring hardware.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹5,000, while another entry records Fifteen hundred rupees.
FY2032 revenue: ₹10 Cr (0.9% of the plan, also listed as ₹10.0 Cr and 0.89% share of group) at 50% gross margin (management projection).
FY2032 volume: 20,000 units, ramping from 200 units in FY27 (management projection).
Mandate schedule: AIS-184 (DDAWS) applies to new models on 1 Oct 2027 and all models on 1 Jan 2028 under CMVR 125Q(1).

radar.lead: The 4D Radar Pod is a sealed automotive radar module delivering range, velocity, azimuth and elevation at ₹25,000 per unit, sold into the aftermarket and integrator channel. Its commercial rationale rests on a single engineering fact: the R100 radar block is designed into the SoC2 die, so the one tapeout that carries the portfolio carries it too.

useCases.title: Fleet radar upgrade on camera-only fitments
useCases.buyer: Fleets and integrators adding radar to camera-only fitments
useCases.problem: Camera-only ADAS systems cannot measure closing speed directly and degrade in rain, dust and glare, conditions common in Indian commercial-vehicle operations, leaving braking decisions based on estimated rather than measured data.
useCases.delivers: The pod mounts forward or on a corner and feeds range, velocity and elevation tracks to the compute box; the R100 block on the SoC2 die fuses those tracks with the camera object list so that closing speed, the quantity a braking decision actually turns on, is measured, not estimated.

useCases.title: Adverse-weather surround sensing in integrated truck kits
useCases.buyer: OEM cab and body engineers and Tier-1 integrators
useCases.problem: Full-surround ADAS kits for commercial vehicles require a sensor channel that continues to function when cameras degrade; front and rear radar coverage must be fused with multiple camera streams within a single frame budget.
useCases.delivers: The pod provides front and rear 4D 77 GHz radar inputs that the SoC2 fuses with seven RGB and two thermal cameras in 8.6 ms of the 33.3 ms frame, supplying animal and cyclist detection in adverse conditions as part of a complete surround-coverage architecture.

useCases.title: Defensible braking-decision sensor for regulated applications
useCases.buyer: Fleet safety officers and integrators where braking decisions must be defensible
useCases.problem: Where a collision event is reviewed after the fact, a closing-speed figure derived from camera estimation may not withstand scrutiny; operators and integrators need a measured value from a dedicated sensor.
useCases.delivers: The radar measures closing speed directly, a quantity a camera estimates and a radar measures, and holds tracks across frames including through rain and dust, providing a recorded, sensor-derived input that supports post-event review.

sections.label: How it works
sections.text: The pod illuminates the forward scene and reads the returns; the R100 radar DSP block on the SoC2 die converts those returns into range, velocity and elevation. Tracks are formed and held across frames, including through rain and dust, which is precisely where camera channels degrade. Those tracks are then fused with the camera object list to confirm or reject detections, with closing speed as the decisive output. The radar front-end and antenna are external components requiring qualification; the DSP processing is on DeepGrid's own silicon.

sections.label: Why now
sections.text: Fleets and integrators are actively adding radar to camera-only fitments as awareness grows that cameras alone cannot supply a measured closing speed in adverse conditions. The AEBS braking piece under AIS-162/IS-11852 was deferred to 1 October 2027, which aligns with the pod's FY2027 first-revenue date and gives integrators a defined compliance window to plan sensor upgrades. The global 4D imaging radar market is sized at $2.75 billion in 2025 with a 13% CAGR according to Business Research Co./Mordor, providing a large demand pool against which the FY2032 volume of 3,000 units represents a 0.03% capture, described by management as runway rather than ceiling, with the near-term serviceable market being the India slice. Pool sizes are third-party published estimates; capture rates are management assumptions.

sections.label: How it makes money
sections.text: The pod is priced at ₹25,000 and sold through aftermarket and integrator supply channels, with management projecting ₹7.5 Cr revenue at 3,000 units by FY2032 at a 50% gross margin. The sensors segment gross margin starts at 30% in FY2027, reflecting hardware bill-of-materials and assembly costs, and rises to 50% by FY2032 as volume grows and supplier terms improve. The product's financial justification within the portfolio is explicit: the radar block is on the same die as the rest of the portfolio, so one tapeout carries all fifteen products, so incremental revenue from the pod carries no additional silicon development cost. At ₹7.5 Cr it is the smallest line in the plan at 0.7% of group FY2032 revenue, and its role is described as supporting the flagship compute products rather than carrying the plan independently.

sections.label: What has to go right
sections.text: Radar front-end supply and antenna qualification are the stated dependencies; the DSP processing is on DeepGrid's own silicon and is not at risk. Verification of the radar block on the ASIC must complete before the product can ship, making that milestone a gating item for FY2027 first revenue. Volume ramps from 30 units in FY2027 to 3,000 in FY2032, so the business depends on integrators and fleets committing to radar upgrades at scale rather than treating the pod as a one-off addition. Because the pod is sold as a component into integrators' safety cases rather than as a complete system, DeepGrid does not own homologation or the braking safety case, which bounds both the liability and the addressable scope.

facts.text: Unit price: ₹25,000 per pod, sold through aftermarket and integrator channels.
FY2032 revenue: ₹7.5 Cr (management projection) at 3,000 units and 50% gross margin, representing 0.7% of group plan revenue.

Demand pool: 4D imaging radar market $2.75 billion globally in 2025 at 13% CAGR (source: Business Research Co./Mordor); FY2032 volume of 3,000 units equals 0.03% capture, a management assumption against a third-party pool estimate.
Fusion budget: SoC2 fuses seven RGB, two thermal and front/rear 4D radar in 8.6 ms of the 33.3 ms frame, leaving 74% headroom.

Road Autonomy.lead: Road Autonomy is DeepGrid Semi's largest product line, comprising three retrofit kits, Smart Truck (AD2 kit), AD0 Smart Mirror, and AD1 Indoor L4 Kit, sold primarily to commercial-vehicle fleet operators and logistics customers in outdoor and indoor operating domains. The line is projected to reach ₹762 Cr in FY2032, representing 67.5% of plan revenue (management projection), anchored by Smart Truck (AD2 kit) at ₹450 Cr and AD0 Smart Mirror at ₹270 Cr, both with first revenue in FY2027.

Silicon & Compute.lead: Silicon & Compute is DeepGrid Semi's semiconductor and compute-module product line, supplying bare SoC2 die to OEM board designers and a tiered family of A100 compute boxes, in M.2, dual-channel, and four-channel PCIe configurations, alongside an AI software licence, to customers ranging from chipset integrators to industrial and infrastructure system builders who embed perception capability into their own products. The line is projected (management projection) to reach ₹194.3 Cr in FY2032, representing 17.2% of plan revenue.

Fleet & Mobility.lead: Fleet & Mobility is DeepGrid Semi's two-SKU line comprising Autonomous TaaS, a contracted autonomous transport operation where DeepGrid owns and operates the vehicle, and Seaport AGV, an autonomous container-yard vehicle sold into port terminals; buyers are logistics operators evaluating cost-per-tonne-kilometre and port authorities automating container yards. Management projects the line will reach a FY2032 total of ₹88.6 Cr, representing 7.9% of plan revenue.

Sensors & Robotics.lead: Sensors & Robotics is DeepGrid Semi's line of perception hardware and autonomous-platform products, spanning defence unmanned ground vehicles, drone compute kits, thermal cameras, driver monitors, and 4D radar pods, sold to defence procurement agencies, commercial-vehicle OEMs, fleet operators, and airframe builders. The line is projected to reach ₹83.5 Cr in FY2032, representing 7.4% of plan revenue (management projection), with first revenues beginning FY2027 across four of its five members and FY2028 for the D100 Drone SoC Kit. Within the plan, it extends DeepGrid Semi's SoC2 silicon into outdoor robotics and sensing domains, opening procurement cycles in both regulated automotive safety mandates and defence logistics.
